about: workflow:keep-jobs-handed-between-ais: keeps the AI and job records that a person's AIs hand each other, in the person's own store, each write made only when its record is still as it was read. It replaces the records-door writes that tool:hand-a-job-to-an-ai, tool:take-an-ai-job, tool:change-an-ai-job and tool:finish-an-ai-job made (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do): those tools keep the work's rules and answer their writes as keep, and this recipe applies them.

payload.label: Keep the jobs my AIs hand each other
payload.job: Keep the AI records and the job records the person's AIs hand each other in the person's own store, so that each job is taken by exactly one AI and every change of a job is written once, against the job as it was read.
payload.produces: The store's own objects for ai and ai-job records, proven on the example attempts: a job written only when its id is absent, a change written only when the job is still as it was read (a refused write means it changed), and a batch all or nothing.

source.from: tools/hand-work-to-ais (read-data/ai-work.mjs and read-data/ai-work.json, and the keep list each of its tool rows answers) on trillion-workshop origin/main, read 2026-11-19 CST.
source.note: Only the keeping is the store's job: a record, its version, and a write made only when the record is absent or still as it was read, in one transaction. The rules of who may take, finish, release or withdraw a job, and the stale-take time, are the tool's values (read-data/ai-work.json), not the store's. The records door and its runner are not used by the keeping; the tool reads its records from input.records and answers its writes as keep.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

tool.description: The tool row to run over the store: tool:hand-a-job-to-an-ai, tool:take-an-ai-job, tool:change-an-ai-job, tool:finish-an-ai-job or tool:see-my-ais; its input is given as input

input.description: That tool's input, without records (this recipe reads them from the store)

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the AI and job records are already kept (kept_in, or null) and the names of the objects that already keep them.

steps.title: Make the store's own objects, once
steps.do: When the look step found nothing, make the store's own objects in its own form: records (id unique, type, value as a JSON object, version starting at 1 and rising by one with each write). A write is made in one transaction only when the record is absent (expected null) or its current value is the value it was read at (the same JSON); otherwise it is a conflict and nothing changes. A batch makes all its writes, and checks all their conditions, in one transaction; if any conflicts, the whole batch is refused and nothing changes. Submit the names of the objects made, or the ones the look step found.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway copy of the same kind of store, with the same objects, run the example attempts in order, each through the store's own objects: (1) seed three AIs ai:north, ai:south and ai:east, each written only if absent (expected null): applied. (2) run tool:hand-a-job-to-an-ai as ai:east, job "Water the plants", to ai:north, key p-one, with the records read from the store as input.records: status written with 1 keep write; apply the keep: applied. (3) the same run again: status written with 0 keep writes. (4) the same key with other words, "Something else": status already-there with 0 keep writes. (5) send p-two from ai:east, "Rename the photos", and apply it. (6) two takes of ai-job:p-two, as ai:north and as ai:south, computed from the same read: applying the first gives applied, applying the second gives conflict and writes nothing. (7) read the store again: tool:take-an-ai-job as ai:south with no id finds nothing to take. (8) tool:change-an-ai-job as ai:east, withdraw of ai-job:p-one (its sender, waiting): moved true, its keep applied. (9) tool:see-my-ais over the store again: ai:north has busy 1. (10) final statuses: ai-job:p-one withdrawn, ai-job:p-two taken with taker ai:north. The same attempts run in the folder's test test/keep-jobs-stores.test.mjs (tools/hand-work-to-ais), on PGlite and on a folder of JSON files; both must give these answers.

answers.description: The answer of each attempt, numbered as in the prove step

steps.title: Keep the jobs this run hands
steps.do: Each time the work runs: read the ai and ai-job records the tool needs from the store (the AIs, and the jobs the call names or lists) and give them to the tool as input.records; run the tool row over that input; then apply its keep list to the store in order, in one transaction, each write only if its record still has the expected value (null: the record must not exist; a null value removes the record). If a write is refused, the job changed since it was read: read again and decide again with the tool; nothing of that run is kept. Submit each job id written, applied, and each refused write with its id and why.

written.description: Each job id written or applied

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes an ai-job record; a job that is gone is not taken again, and an AI record is removed only by the person's own edit.
